topic: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
syllabus_extract: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
specific_objectives: 11.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the properties of atmosphere, flow over bodies, boundary layer.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of Pitot-Static tube installation; Safety: Ensure no loose parts; Supervision: Instructor monitors probe alignment.
intro_questions: What is the definition of static pressure?
How does dynamic pressure relate to airspeed?
What is the function of the pitot-static system?

development.content:
Definition of static pressure
Definition of dynamic pressure
Definition of total pressure
Bernoulli's principle application
Pitot-static tube operation

Indicated airspeed definition
Rectified airspeed correction
Equivalent airspeed calculation
True airspeed derivation
Altitude and temperature effects

Position error sources
Instrument error types
Compressibility error impact
Calibration procedures
Error correction methods

summary_questions: Explain the relationship between indicated and true airspeed.
Identify two common sources of ASI error.
Describe how temperature affects equivalent airspeed.
home_assignment_question: Review the definition of streamline and stream tube from the previous lesson plan to understand flow characteristics relevant to pressure distribution.

pft_rows.syllabus: Definition of streamline, stream tube, stream filament, ideal and real fluid, steady and turbulent flow, compressible and incompressible flow, viscous and in viscous flow, rotational and irrotational flow.
